st: Simmer the chicken in the [[4 cups]] broth with [[1 tsp]] salt for 25 minutes in a large pot. Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until they pop and turn lightly golden. Move to a bowl, then toast the sesame seeds and cinnamon stick for 1 minute.
In the same pan, char the tomatoes, tomatillos, onion, garlic and chilies for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until blistered and soft.
Blend the toasted seeds, charred vegetables, cinnamon and peppercorns with [[2 cups]] of the warm broth until very smooth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in the pot, pour in the sauce (it will spatter) and cook 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the remaining broth, potatoes, chayote and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Return the chicken and simmer another 10 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C). Add water if too thick.
Serve in bowls with rice and warm tortillas.
Put the turkey, half the onion, [[2 tsp]] salt and [[8 cups]] water in a large pot. Boil, skim the foam, then simmer for 1 hour until tender.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat and char the tomatoes, remaining onion, bell pepper, garlic and chilies for 8 minutes, turning, until blistered.
Blend the charred vegetables, achiote and [[2 cups]] of the turkey broth until smooth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pot, pour in the sauce and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until it deepens in color.
Add the sauce to the turkey broth along with the ginger and mint. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the cilantro bunch and simmer 5 minutes more, then remove the cilantro and mint stems.
Taste and add salt. Serve the turkey in bowls with the red broth, with rice or tamalitos on the side.
Simmer the chicken in [[3 cups]] broth with [[1 tsp]] salt for 25 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Lift out the chicken and keep the broth.
Toast the pumpkin seeds and sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 minutes until golden.
Boil the tomatillos and chilies in water for 8 minutes until olive-colored and soft. Drain.
Blend the tomatillos, chilies, seeds, cilantro, green onions, garlic, torn tortilla and [[1.5 cups]] of broth until smooth.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large pot. Pour in the green sauce and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often.
Add the chicken and the rest of the broth. Simmer for 15 minutes until the sauce is thick.
Season with salt and serve with white rice and tortillas.
Put the beef in a pot with half the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[6 cups]] water. Boil, skim the foam, then simmer covered for 1 hour 30 minutes until very tender.
Lift the beef out, keep [[3 cups]] of the broth, and shred the meat with two forks into thin strands (hilachas means rags).
Char the tomatoes, tomatillos, remaining onion, garlic and chilies in a dry skillet for 8 minutes, turning.
Blend the charred vegetables with the cinnamon and [[1 cup]] of the broth until smooth.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot, add the sauce and cook for 10 minutes, stirring, until thick and darker.
Add the shredded beef, remaining broth, potatoes, carrots and [[1 tsp]] salt. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the green beans if using and simmer 5 more minutes until the vegetables are tender. Serve with rice.

ing: half chopped, half in the sauce
st: Char the peppers over a flame or under the broiler for 10 minutes, turning, until blackened. Cover in a bowl for 10 minutes, peel, then cut a slit down one side and remove the seeds.

Cook the pork in a pan with the chopped onion for 8 minutes, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 160°F (71°C). Add the carrots, green beans, [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper and cook 8 minutes.
Simmer the tomatoes, remaining onion, garlic and broth for 15 minutes, then blend smooth with [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Keep warm in a pot.
Stuff each pepper with the filling and close the slit, using a toothpick if needed. Dust lightly with [[0.5 cup]] flour.
Beat the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form, then fold in the yolks gently.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a skillet to 350°F (175°C). Dip each pepper into the egg batter and fry 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain.
Simmer the fried peppers in the tomato sauce for 5 minutes to warm through.
Serve hot with the sauce spooned over.
Simmer the pork in water with half the onion, [[1 tsp]] salt and 2 cloves garlic for 1 hour until tender. Keep [[2 cups]] of the broth, then shred or dice the pork.
Char the tomatoes, remaining onion, garlic and chilies in a dry skillet for 8 minutes. Blend with [[1 cup]] of the pork broth into a smooth sauce.
Cook the sauce in a pot with [[2 tbsp]] oil for 10 minutes, then mix in the pork, capers and raisins.

Make the masa: beat [[0.5 cup]] lard or oil into the masa harina, then slowly add [[3 cups]] warm broth and [[1.5 tsp]] salt to make a soft, spreadable dough. Mix in about half the red sauce for color.
Warm the banana leaves over a flame for 20 seconds until shiny and flexible.
Spread about a third of a cup of masa on a leaf. Add a spoon of pork sauce and an olive, then fold the leaf over and wrap into a tidy parcel. Tie with string.
Arrange the tamales in a steamer basket over simmering water.
Cover and steam for 1 hour 15 minutes, topping up the water as needed, until the masa pulls cleanly from the leaf.
Rest 10 minutes before unwrapping.
Simmer the chicken in water with [[1 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Keep [[1 cup]] of the broth. Shred the chicken.
Char the tomatoes, garlic, onion and chilies in a dry skillet for 8 minutes. Blend with the [[1 cup]] of chicken broth into a smooth sauce.
Simmer the sauce in a pot for 10 minutes and stir in the shredded chicken. Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Beat the lard or oil into the masa harina, then add [[3 cups]] warm broth and [[1 tsp]] salt to make a soft, spreadable dough.
Soak the husks in hot water for 20 minutes until pliable, then pat dry.
Spread about a third of a cup of masa in the middle of a husk. Add a spoon of chicken sauce and a strip of cheese.
Fold the husk around the filling into a parcel, fold the narrow end up, and tie with a strip of husk.
Stand the chuchitos upright in a steamer over simmering water. Cover and steam for 1 hour until the masa is firm.
Rest 10 minutes and serve with extra sauce.

ing: hot dog buns or small baguettes
st: Boil or grill the hot dogs until hot all the way through, about 5 minutes.
Butter the insides of the buns and toast them cut side down in a skillet for 1 minute until golden.
Spread each bun with [[1 tbsp]] mayonnaise on one side.
Place a hot dog in each bun.
Spoon about [[0.25 cup]] guacamole over each.
Top with cabbage, tomato and onion.
Finish with a zigzag of ketchup and mustard and serve right away.
Boil the beets for 40 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Cool, peel and dice. Boil the carrots, green beans, cauliflower and peas until just tender, about 8 minutes, then drain.
Make the pickling dressing: stir [[1 cup]] vinegar, [[1 cup]] water, [[0.25 cup]] sugar, [[2 tsp]] salt, [[0.33 cup]] oil and the mustard until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cooked vegetables with the dressing in a large bowl.
Cover and chill the vegetables for at least 2 hours (traditionally overnight) so they pick up the flavor.
Drain off most of the liquid and keep it in a jar.
Add the ham, salami, chicken and cheese cubes and the pickled onions. Mix gently.
Pile on a large platter and decorate with the egg quarters and some of the colorful vegetables.
Serve cold, adding a spoonful of the dressing if it seems dry.
Peel the plantains, cut in chunks, and boil in water for 15 minutes until very soft. Drain well.
Mash the plantains in a bowl with the flour and salt until a smooth, soft dough forms. Cover and set aside.
Make the filling: mash the beans with a fork. Put them in a pan with [[0.25 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon, chocolate and water.
Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes, stirring, until it is a thick, smooth paste. Cool completely.
With wet hands, scoop about 2 tablespoons of plantain dough into your palm and flatten it.
Add a spoonful of bean filling and fold the dough over it, sealing into an oval or ball with no gaps.
Heat [[1.5 cups]] oil in a deep skillet to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rellenitos in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until dark golden. Drain on paper towels.
Dust with powdered sugar if you like and serve warm.
